findings.title: Drain filtered terminal replies before declaring recovery ready
findings.impact: Queued input from a disconnected or not-yet-presented attachment can be interpreted as a deliberate ownership gesture on the fresh controller. A surviving prefix/Ctrl-L sequence emits a new cooperative claim, creating a reservation or immediately acquiring an unowned ACP target, contrary to the required no-replay/no-implicit-acquisition recovery boundary.
findings.evidence: The new recovery loop breaks on event::poll(Duration::ZERO) == false at src/tui.rs:1287–1288 and uses another such probe at line 1299 before eventually clearing drain_recovered_input. In vendor/crossterm/src/event/read.rs:60–89, a zero-time poll returns false after one nonmatching internal event, even when the source has further events queued. EventFilter rejects cursor-position/device replies (src/event/filter.rs:48–56); the Unix parser produces InternalEvent::CursorPosition for ESC[row;colR (src/event/sys/unix/parse.rs:241–256), and the mio Parser retains subsequent events. For example, while recovery registration is held, queue three cursor-position replies followed by the old prefix/Ctrl-L gesture: the pre-view probe, drain probe and final probe can each consume one reply and return false, leaving the ownership keys behind when readiness is enabled. Those keys then reach src/tui.rs:1451–1460, NativeControl::open/request at src/tui/control.rs:934–975, and Work::Claim, whose consuming ownership dispatch creates a real claim. This is a new dependence of recovery on an inherited reader behavior, not a request to fix an unrelated pre-existing terminal feature.
findings.fix: Provide a bounded drain/probe that distinguishes actual source exhaustion from encountering a filtered internal event. Continue through immediately available internal/parser events, preserve the no-parent-fd-flag-mutation property, and remain fail-closed if the drain budget is exhausted rather than reporting an empty queue. Use that result before clearing drain_recovered_input. Extend the held-registration controlling-PTY regression with cursor-position/device replies before stale ownership shortcuts; assert zero claims/reservations and unchanged owner/work, then verify a separately entered fresh gesture works.

summary: FAIL: one supported P1 must-fix recovery-input defect. The checklist passes 34 of 36 items, so the computed score is 100 × 34 / 36 = 94.44444444444444; meeting the numeric threshold does not satisfy the zero-must-fix security gate. The remaining reviewed launch, settings, identity, ownership and cleanup paths did not yield another patch-introduced actionable defect.
limits: Independent read-only static source/security review only. No edits, builds, tests, lint, formatters, executable/source execution, providers, auth/config/global operations or commits were performed. No prior review/audit/runtime/handoff reports, actual credentials or retired private fixtures were read; PLAN.md was limited to lines 1–45. Test descriptions above refer to inspected assertions, not exercised results. The 57 unchanged vendor files were treated according to the sealed released-source provenance and inspected for integration, not independently re-certified as a newly audited upstream release. Frozen hashes were not independently recomputed. This review does not establish runtime/provider acceptance, installed-source equivalence, or approval of fixture evidence as a substitute for genuine same-instance OMP effects. Historical unknown native application settlement remains unsafe and was neither reclassified as a new defect nor waived into acceptance.
